newsitem.title: USA: Clinton does not want forex used for trade gains.
newsitem.headline: Clinton does not want forex used for trade gains.

text.p: President Clinton said Friday he does not believe foreign currency exchange markets should be used to gain undue advantage in global trade.
"We do not want a weak dollar simply to improve our trade position," Clinton said at a joint news conference with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
"That is not our economic policy to go out and seek a weak dollar," Clinton said. He added the United States wants a strong, healthy dollar, which reflects its strong economy.
"But neither do we want any other actions to have the effect of throwing the exchange rate system out of whack in order to gain undue advantage in international trade," Clinton said.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin voiced concern on Friday about the weak yen. In a briefing with reporters, he also reiterated that U.S. dollar policy remained unchanged.
